parts: Not sure if this is correct, but I don't think you can use

template <class Type>
Type testing(int i1, int i2, int i3, double x, vector<Type> y, vector<Type> newknots)

with testing(2,2,1,1.7252021,x,boundaryknots) because (I think) "x" and "boundaryknots" are not the same Type. Thus the compiler error(s). Might try redefining "testing" as
template <class T1, Type>
Type testing(int i1, int i2, int i3, double x, vector<T1> y, vector<Type> newknots)

or something similar. 

Also, note that you don't actually use "y" anywhere in the body of "testing" (yet).

I apologise, the correct syntax for a template with 2 different types (e.g., double and CppAD...) is
template <class T1, class T2>
NOT 
template <class T1, T2> as implied by my answer the other day (missing the "class" qualifier on the second type.

Note that "T1" and "T2" are just stand-ins (i.e., template <class T1, class Type> would also be valid).

The following has a nice introduction to templates that I found helpful (but it doesn't cover multiple type templates)
http://www.cplusplus.com/doc/oldtutorial/templates/

a post which does address multiple types in a template is:
